newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen up on crude gains/Iraqi news.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen up on crude gains/Iraqi news.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Monday were expected to end firmer on crude gains and higher paper swaps levels amid fresh Iraqi news, traders said.
"Physical cash prices are likely to end firmer as crude rise on fresh Iraqi news," said a trader.
Latest news from Baghdad reported that anti-Baghdad Kurdish rebels have regained two more towns from its pro-Baghdad rivals, after seizing the Kurd's biggest town, Sulaimaniya, on Sunday.
October paper swaps levels were also higher to bid at $119.50, from Friday's $119-$120 per tonne.
An offer was seen for 180-cst cargoes at $122 for early November loading, a trader said.
He said while prices will rise, the physical market remained long. "There are adequate supplies," said a trader.
He said term demand from Vietnam in the fourth quarter and China will provide further support.
Offers into China were heard at $8 per tonne over Singapore spot quotes c+f southern China.
